hook: Myth: your landlord's insurance covers your stuff.

blocks.narration: Myth: your landlord's insurance covers your stuff. Fact: it usually covers the building itself, not the belongings inside your apartment.
blocks.visual: A clay apartment building under a protective dome, but the furniture inside sits outside the dome

blocks.narration: If a fire, burst pipe, or break-in damages your things, the landlord's policy usually will not pay to replace them.
blocks.visual: A miniature clay apartment with a dripping pipe soaking a tiny couch and laptop

blocks.narration: Renters insurance covers your personal property, and many policies cover it even outside your home, like a laptop stolen from your car.
blocks.visual: A small dome now surrounds the laptop, following it into a tiny clay car

blocks.narration: It usually includes liability coverage too. If a guest slips and gets hurt in your place, it can help pay for that.
blocks.visual: A clay figure slips on a tiny rug while a soft cushion appears beneath them

blocks.narration: Many policies also pay for extra living costs, like a hotel, if your apartment becomes unlivable after a covered disaster.
blocks.visual: A tiny clay suitcase rolls toward a small hotel with a glowing sign

blocks.narration: For all that protection, renters insurance often costs less each month than a couple of streaming subscriptions put together.
blocks.visual: Two tiny streaming remotes balance on a scale against a small house-shaped shield

blocks.narration: Check two things when you buy: replacement cost versus actual cash value, and whether expensive items need extra coverage.
blocks.visual: A magnifying glass hovers over a clay policy document with two glowing lines

blocks.narration: It is one of the cheapest protections you can buy as a renter. Tag a friend who rents and does not have this.
blocks.visual: The protective dome expands to cover the whole apartment and everything inside

cta: Tag a friend who rents and does not have this.

captions.hook_line: Your landlord's insurance doesn't cover your stuff. This does 🏠
captions.body: Renters insurance typically covers your belongings (often even outside the home), liability if someone is hurt, and extra living costs if your place becomes unlivable. A landlord's policy covers the building, not your things. Check your own policy's limits.

youtube_title: Renters Insurance Covers More Than You Think
